areas.title: The person says when a session starts: only Start, Approve and start, Continue, Use API key on a credential card, 'run it now' in chat (always read back once), a schedule they set, or the project's 'Start a session by itself' starts one; every answer, Tasks-row action, chat change, budget raise or reset, returning credential and CI or PR event only prepares work, which joins the running session if it fits its promise (option C), else waits for the next Start, said in one line; a credential stop's end prepares too, and the session's Continue (or 'Start at 15:40' pressed before) carries what is left of its promise and budget; quiet hours hold every other start without losing it; edits apply before a task starts

[question] D6-15: The critic's monthly calibration is a session nobody pressed Start for (on by default, a 'schedule' session on no project that spends on the model within its own cap); it does no project work, but the rule 'only the person starts a session' must name it; Owner's words: "the user clearly states when a session will run"; Where: jobs/calibration.ts:60-67, :285-300; ADR 0060; settings-view.ts:177-179.
decisions: S-1 Who asked is on every start: StartRequest.by = 'person' | 'schedule' | 'hands_off' (append-only; continues?: the session id a person start continues; trigger stays for the record), written on the session.started event and in the session row's plan JSON (plan.startedBy, append-only, no migration), which d1109-sessions words. Person starts: POST /sessions, session.start (chat, voice and phone), Approve and start (intake), Approve and start on the level 0/1 session plan card, Continue on a budget card, Use API key on a credential card (personStart / personContinue, called by d1109-cred-engine), Continue where it stopped, a session's Continue, the recovery Update's Continue, and a person start kept for a credential's reset. The daemon's Scheduler gets isQuietHours from a cached reader (QuietHours in compose.ts: notify_prefs.quiet_hours and the time zone, refreshed in the scheduler's refresh hook before every tick and when the settings route changes them; the port reads it synchronously); deferredNow holds every start that is not by 'person'; enqueue keeps every person start; a schedule's fired key is written when its start leaves the waiting line (started, or queued behind a session), never while quiet hours hold it. The critic's calibration is named in the ADR as the one exception (by 'schedule', as today). Why: the owner's control needs one fact the scheduler can enforce; the Quiet hours setting promises 'no sessions that start on their own'; a job held in the night must still run once.

S-2 One function prepares work: prepareWork(deps, {agentId, projectId, taskIds, reason, by: 'person' | 'system' | 'agent'}) in a new session/prepared-work.ts replaces resumeWork's start in every answer path (person-questions, cannot-run, findings, pr-answers rebase and Redo, late approvals) and returns {outcome, line}; recordStart stores the outcome on the card for its Done line. Outcomes: joined, no_room, stopping, waits_start, stopped_all, started, queued, deferred, nothing_to_run, failed. Why: one place decides and one map of words says it (design §5 rule 10), so no answer path starts a session by its own logic again.

S-3 Budget raises and resets prepare: wakeBudgetWaits withdraws the card and makes the task ready, then calls prepareWork (by 'system') instead of resumeWork; a raise through Settings (monthly cap, project budget, the subscription's allowance, whose share stop is d1109-cred-engine's) runs the wake at once and its change line says how many paused tasks are ready again and that they run at the next Start. Continue on a budget card stays a person start (personStart with the card's budget). Why: the owner: 'the user clearly states when a session will run'; a month reset can come weeks later, in the middle of the person's instructions.

S-4 CI results and PR comments start nothing, with the setting on or off: GitHostWatcher.fire no longer asks the scheduler; the events are delivered to the agent's inbox as today (deliver), the audit row records outcome 'waits_start', and the next session's brief reads them. Why: no start nobody asked for, and text a third party wrote never starts paid work; the information still reaches the next session (ADR 0075's content rule unchanged); whether the hands-off setting should let them start one is an owner question.

S-5 The hands-off setting: project.settings.start_by_itself, false by default for every project (no migration: absent is off); settings-view row 'When work is ready' with 'Wait for my Start' / 'Start a session by itself'; SETTING_SPECS entry (scope project, risk medium, narrows when off; turning on asks the yes with its effect line 'Sessions of Quote page will start by themselves when work you made ready can run, up to CHF 5.00 each. Never in your quiet hours or while sessions are stopped.'); settings.set refuses it for an agent actor. prepareWork and the budget and credential wakes read it; a start it makes is by 'hands_off', only for preparation by 'person' or 'system' (never by 'agent': D7's own tasks), with the project's session cap, after startBlocked (Stop all, no Claude, nothing runnable). A hands-off start held by quiet hours or queued behind another start is kept on the project (summary_cache.start_pending {since, why}, version-checked), asked again by a sweep in the scheduler's refresh hook once nothing holds it (after a restart too), and cleared when it starts. Why: the owner confirmed 'Only when you say so' as the default with the hands-off setting optional; per project so one project can run hands-off while another is shaped; a line that says 'It runs after your quiet hours.' must stay true across a Quit.

S-6 The promise is the Start dialog's list: promiseOf(check) in start-check.ts = runnable (cut as today) then later cut to the work budget left after runnable, in run order (the followers beyond it are named 'and N more wait for a later Start'); the runner computes the promise with the same function at its start (or takes the approved plan's tasks and followers, or, for a session's Continue, the remaining promise of the session it continues), emits session.promised {taskIds, estimateUsdMicro} and keeps it on the plan row. The dialog's sentence reads the cut list and adds one line 'Work you make ready while it runs joins it if its budget has room.'; while another project's session runs, 'Starts after the session on "Quote page"'. Why: 'the session keeps its promise' needs the promise to be what the person saw when they pressed Start.

S-7 Join only if it fits: a live-session registry (new session/live-sessions.ts) where the runner registers an admit handle for its project. admit(taskIds, by) reads each task fresh: the session's own (promised and runnable by itself, or waiting for its Claude credential inside the session) -> joined; stopping, wrapping up, in its end review or closing -> stopping (the line 'Ready: it runs at your next Start.'; the task is added to notAgain so it does not run in that session); an oversized task (estimate above the whole work budget, D4) -> no_room; else room = work budget less spent less the remaining estimates of its own tasks and of what joined; estimate (priced as the planner prices) <= room -> joined (kept in the session's joined map, session.joined event), else no_room. closing: when the queue is empty the runner sets the handle's closing flag before its last replan and clears it only if that replan found work, so an admit between an empty replan and the session's end never answers joined. readmit(taskIds) takes credential-waiting tasks back as the session's own and clears notAgain for them (d1109-cred-engine's Use API key). A task the person pauses or cancels, or that needs the person's answer, gives its room back; bringing it back is a newcomer. D7's changes: the parts of a split promised task are the session's own up to the task's remaining estimate (a part beyond it is a newcomer); a step added before a promised task is a newcomer, and if it does not fit the promised task leaves the promise and both are named once in the result; a dropped duplicate frees its room; the task check's cost is admitted like a newcomer (room after the promise and what joined). replan takes its own tasks first, then joined, then newcomers re-admitted in priority order after each task ends; nothing else (today's 'every ready task that fits'). At levels 0 and 1 a person's preparation is added to onlyThese when it joins; anything the agent adds is not. The result's 'Left for your next Start: ...' and two log lines (event-lines.ts) say it. Why: option C keeps the promise and uses spare budget; deciding at the action makes the line true; admitting never raises a budget.

S-8 Edits apply before a task starts and never during its run: at the claim the runner refreshes the queue item from the claimed row (specialist, title, estimate re-priced) before chooseSpecialist and the start line; task.update of a running task keeps refusing its field changes but queues the note it carries and answers '"X" is running now: it is not changed mid-run; your note goes into its next attempt.' (today the refusal drops the note). Why: 'queue up tasks and then change things': a change made before the run must be the run; a change mid-run would mix two briefs.

S-9 Every preparing action says what happens next: the commands that make a task ready (task.transition to ready, task.resume, task.reopen, task.create with status ready, which Make this a task uses) call ports.prepareWork after their transaction and append its line to the sentence (the Tasks row shows change.sentence already, chat replies with it); chat's read-back of such a move adds a preview of the line (ports.previewWork, read-only). The Inbox's card explains are read when the card is shown: RequestWordsContext gains running ('this_project' | 'other' | null) and startsByItself, so Try again reads '...; it joins the running session if it fits.' or '...; it runs at your next Start.'. Make ready's and Resume's static explains become 'Ready to run: the running session takes it if it fits, else your next Start.' and 'It is ready again: the running session takes it if it fits, else your next Start.'. Why: design §5 rule 4 (true now) and rule 9 (no promise the code does not keep); the owner wants to know when a session will run.

S-10 A credential stop's end prepares, and the person continues: the executor's noteWait passes the session id and the wait entry stores it ({projectId, agentId, since, sessionId}); at the stop's end credentialWaits.wake takes the entry and calls prepareWork(by 'system') for its project, so nothing starts unless the hands-off setting is on or a person start is kept on the entry. A person's Start, or a session's Continue, pressed while the stop lasts ('Start at 15:40') keeps one person start on the entry ({by 'person', continues, budgetUsdMicro}, version-checked; keepStartAtReset), made once at the stop's end, after a restart too and never twice; POST /projects/:id/continuation/cancel (Cancel), Stop all and a newer Start of the project drop it. A session's Continue (its page, the project status line, Home) opens the Start dialog with continues = that session: the remaining promise and budgetUsdMicro = its cap less the ledger's booked spend (no Continue when that is zero or less); the runner's first log line 'Goes on with your session of 14:05.'. personContinue(sessionId) and readmit(taskIds) are the ports d1109-cred-engine's Use API key calls. Row and card words: '...; then it runs at your next Start.' / '...; then your session goes on.' (a kept start). What a wait is, which credential serves next and whether the person is asked first stay D5's. Why: the owner's confirmed list puts 'a credential coming back' among what only prepares work; the person's own Continue keeps the promise and the budget they gave; whether a session should go on by itself at the reset is asked.

S-11 Chat says start in words, and every start said in chat or voice is read back: session.start gets askFromChat (a yes from chat and voice at any budget, whether the parser or the chat model asked; the app's, the palette's and the phone's starts are no chat); the parser also maps 'run it now', 'run them now', 'run it', 'go ahead and run it', 'let's run it', 'start it' (and the German 'starte es', 'jetzt ausführen') to session.start; negations ('don't run it yet', 'I'll run it later', 'not yet') and task text ('add a task: run the tests') do not. The chat model's tool definitions change: session.start ('Start a work session now on the person's say-so; it is read back for their yes; answers and task changes never start one'), task.reopen, task.resume and task.transition ('it is ready again: it joins the running session if it fits, else it waits for the person's next Start'), settings_set's new key line. Why: the owner named 'run it now'; 'ok' or 'sounds good' read by a model is not the person stating when a session runs; tool definitions are model-facing code and must say what the app does.

S-12 Words: one map in prepared-work.ts (preparedLine, preparedExplain) used by request-words.ts (startWords and the cards' explains and Done lines), task-words.ts (budget-paused and credential-wait rows), result.ts (paused and credential lines, the left-for-next-Start line), credential-wait.ts (after-the-wait sentences) and the commands' sentences; no person-facing sentence says 'by itself', 'starts a session' or 'goes on' unless the setting, a kept start or the person's own Continue makes it true. Why: design §5 rules 4, 9, 10; the owner: 'a sentence promises only what the app does'.

S-13 The ADR (next free number) records the rule, names the critic's calibration as the one exception, and amends 0053 (Approve and start on a session plan is a person start), 0060 (the calibration named as the exception; schedules held by quiet hours still run once), 0075 (CI and PR comments start no session; they reach the next session), 0088 (a late approval prepares; the next session consumes it), 0100 (a wait's end prepares; a session's Continue carries its remaining promise and budget; a person start kept for the reset), 0102 point 2 (Tasks-row actions prepare), 0112 (a raised or reset limit prepares; Continue is a person start), each amendment dated. Why: AGENTS.md: decisions go in ADRs; the session lead edits design core-experience.md from design_doc_changes.
u_entries: new (session lead): 'Sessions start when I did not press Start' (answers, raises, a credential back, PR comments) with this area's Check in the app steps
root_causes: packages/runtime/src/session/resume-work.ts: one helper starts (or queues) a session for every answer that makes a task runnable; every answer path calls it, so preparing work and starting work are the same act.

packages/runtime/src/session/triggers.ts and daemon/compose.ts: a start request carries only its trigger kind, not who asked, and the daemon's Scheduler is built without quiet hours, so a person's start and an automatic one are treated alike and the Quiet hours promise is not kept.

packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts: the session has no promise (replan takes whatever ready task fits the room left), no way for an action outside the runner to ask whether a task may join, and it runs the plan's snapshot of a task's specialist and estimate.
packages/runtime/src/wiring/billing-pick.ts and daemon/compose.ts: a credential wait is kept per project without the session it belongs to, so its end can only start a fresh, full-budget session.
packages/runtime/src/session/githost-watcher.ts and session/budget-card.ts: automatic producers call the scheduler directly.
The words: request-words.ts, task-words.ts, result.ts, credential-wait.ts and the commands each wrote their own 'starts a session' / 'goes on by itself' sentence for one behaviour.
packages/commands/src/commands/session.ts: session.start is read back only above a money line, so a start said in chat, or asked by the chat model, acts at once below it.
packages/runtime/src/session/triggers.ts: a schedule's fired key is written before its start and a quiet-hours hold lives in memory, so a hold that outlives the process loses the start.

S-10 composed cases in the credential-wait tests with the stand-in subscription and the simulated clock (the stop's end prepares; the session's Continue with its budget from the ledger; a start kept by Start before the reset; the cancel route; Stop all; a newer Start; the setting on; a legacy entry) and a compose-twice restart case before the reset (one kept start, made once; none without it), plus real-daemon cases for POST /sessions with continues and POST /projects/:id/continuation/cancel; S-11 the intent unit, a composed chat case at a CHF 1.00 budget and one where the stand-in chat model calls session_start after 'ok' and after 'sounds good' (nothing starts before Yes; Yes starts one), and the conversation request-builder test asserting the exact tool definitions the model receives; S-12 the unit test of each function that writes a sentence (exact strings, at most 100 characters, CHF, no id) plus a grep test over the words modules for 'by itself', 'starts a session' and 'goes on' outside the true cases; S-13 docs. Every changed or new route gets its real-daemon case and apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts changes in the same commit. Existing tests that assert today's behaviour (answers start sessions: resume-work, plan-approval, budget-pause, credential-limits, credential-wait-session, task-usage-limit, session-keeps-going, sandbox-waiting, subscription-path, signoff-answer, where-last-run-stopped, writing-rules, w15-chat-words, the githost-watcher cases, the UI's inbox, tasks, project and polish-screens tests, real-daemon cases) change with the design, each named in its commit; none is weakened or skipped. Money: admit never raises a budget and never uses the review fifth; a session's Continue (or a kept start) uses the cap less the ledger's booked spend, never more; a hands-off start uses the project's session cap and every outer cap (month, plan share) holds; when a line says it waits, nothing moves (assert no start and no spend). decisions: The check runs on evidence only (a report's 'For the task list:' lines, a review note the task did not cause, notes kept from before), at most once per task boundary and three times a session, never after the wrap-up line. Why: cost; the owner wants fixes 'as part of a run', not a paid replan after every task.

The planning model at one effort step below the intake (medium), 4,096 output tokens, 120 s, a JSON reply and no tools, routed like the intake's planning call, capped at its own estimate inside the session's work budget, a Run row 'task-check' booked in the session. Why: planning quality for a small call; one path on both credentials; money visible and inside the budget.

Five kinds of change, each a registry command (task.update, task.dependencies, task.create with 'then', task.split, task.transition with 'duplicate_of'). Why: every change gets the change log, the version check and a state-based Undo that survives a restart (ADR 0030); no new write path to the store.

A split keeps the task as its first part and adds 1 to 3 new tasks; every criterion goes word for word into a part; a task's own budget is shared, never raised. Why: the folder, branch and earlier work stay; the bar cannot be lowered by splitting; no budget is passed.

New action class plan_fix, free from Standard by the session lead's default (the owner named no level; asked); Advisor and Assisted get one suggestion card. Why: the owner's 'the autonomy level deciding when it asks first'; Standard is the default level, and plan_fix frees only the bounded fixes.

Ask first at every level for flagged input, the person's own task, a criterion removed from a task that ran or has open findings, a deploy or migration step, a question for the person, a new task whose specialist reaches further than its source task's, more than two drops, or an unlike duplicate. Why: these are the changes whose mistake costs the person (their edit lost, the bar lowered, risky work or their time added, work cancelled).

Each change the agent makes alone is one Changes row (source 'session') with one Undo, a line on the session page and no Inbox line; the session's one Update counts them. A set the person approves with one Yes is one row with one Undo. Why: the confirmed 'every change shown with one Undo' and design §3.8's 'What becomes an Update: one line per session'.

Added work joins the running session only by d1109-starts-engine's admit rule: the parts of a split promised task share its remaining estimate, a new task or a step before a promised task joins only if the room after the promise and what joined covers it (else both wait for the next Start, named once), and the check itself is paid only from that room; the agent's preparation never starts a session, the hands-off setting included. Why: D6 (the person says when a session starts) and option C ('the session keeps its promise').

A task with an open card (failed after its tries, needs your answer, paused at a budget) or paused by the person is left alone. Why: the card is the one place for that decision (design §3.8); D4's continuation stays as built.

Evidence goes in the data envelope and is scanned; a flagged line is kept, never sent to the model, and turns the set into a suggestion card that quotes it; a new task's specialist reaches no further than its source task's without a yes; a task written from a report says so in its brief; the strict schema and the fence hold whatever the model returns; the check's run has no tools. Why: a prompt may ask, only code can allow (AGENTS.md); a report must not reach the web through a task it wrote.

decisions: CE-1 One policy: human.notify_prefs.credential_policy, one of subscription_then_wait, subscription_then_ask, subscription_then_key, key_then_subscription, key_only (packages/billing/src/policy.ts: CREDENTIAL_POLICIES; ruleOf(id) = {order, whenStopped: next | ask | wait, kinds}, key_only without the subscription; credentialPolicyOf(prefs) = the stored id, else derived at every read: billing_order with the subscription first + wait or unset -> subscription_then_wait, + use_other -> subscription_then_key, api_key or plan_credits first + use_other -> key_then_subscription, + wait or unset -> {chosen: 'earlier', the stored order, whenStopped wait, both kinds: the chooser keeps running a task only the subscription can do here on it, as today, which key_only would not}, no billing_order -> {chosen: false, the split order (tasks the routing policy's, every other call CALL_FALLBACK_ORDER), whenStopped wait, or next under use_other}; stopKeyOf(source, status); moneyRank, the earlier choice ranked as key_only). Why: the owner's 'a framework for what to use when, and then the system just does it'; read at every pick, so a change applies to the next call; deriving at read changes nothing a person chose and keeps ADR 0100 point 2 for a person who never chose (owner question).

CE-2 The router holds every stop: RouteContext.whenStopped replaces waitOnRest (waitOnRest still read as 'wait' for one release); the held list covers resting (reason limit), refused, plan_share (share, until the next month's start UTC) and monthly_limit (key_month), each with until and stopKey; under ask and wait a held first choice throws unavailable with details.waitFor {sourceId, kind, reason, until, stopKey, ask}; a grant {to, stopKey} on the held source whose stopKey is the current one lets the granted kind serve; a grant never lifts the hold for purpose batch (background jobs); next moves as today; RouteContext.heldNow (sources the caller saw stop on this call) are held like resting ones. Why: one place decides, so every caller agrees (7a, 7b, 7c).

CE-3 RouterTaskBilling.pick reads the policy at every pick for every purpose (session, critic, interactive, which D7's task check uses, chat, batch; a grant covers every purpose but batch); the sources in req.exclude go to the router as heldNow, not as withheld, under ask and wait; at a stop it never moves to a lower chooser group: the task waits with reason needs. Why: one rule for every call; the exclude list today hides the very stop the hold must see; the plan card's 'only it can' stays true (ADR 0100 point 13).

CE-4 RoutedProvider follows the rule: after rest or refuse it picks again under the rule; under ask and wait the call ends with the wait (code unavailable, details.wait), which each caller handles as today: the critic's review waits in review without a counted try (review-refusal.ts), the plan waits (the intake's waitNow), chat holds (CE-9), a job skips (CE-10); under next one move as today, recorded with its cost (CE-11). holdNow(model) beside waitNow says whether a call would be held and whether a one-off switch could serve (for chat and d1109-chat-depth's thorough pass). Why: D5-1 is the main money leak today.

CE-5 A task its credential stopped keeps its work; under next, or after a grant, it goes back to the head of the session's queue and continues on the next credential in the same session; the brief's previous-run section for a usage_limit, credential_refused or share-stopped run is a sibling of whereTheLastRunStopped with exact text ('stopped when its Claude credential reached its limit' / 'was refused' / 'reached the share of the subscription Forerunner may use'), never 'It failed', with its siblings for a run that changed no file ('The last run of this task stopped when its Claude credential reached its limit, before it changed any file.') and for one that left no note ('It left no note: its Claude credential stopped it before it could write one.'); under ask and wait it waits, the session goes on with what can run and ends to wait, and at the stop's end the work is ready for the person's next Start (d1109-starts-engine S-10). Why: 7a ('the task to be completed by the API') without spending twice.

CE-6 Forerunner's share reached mid-run (the hooks' plan level, unchanged) returns as a credential stop with reason share and its handoff kept on the run (read by CE-5's brief): no budget card, the session does not end for it, the rule decides; the stop ends at the month's start or when the person raises the allowance (the share falls under the cap; the stop key changes); its waiting work then reads Ready for the next Start and nothing starts (d1109-starts-engine S-3, S-10). Budget cards at source 'plan' filed before the upgrade keep their wake (wakeBudgetWaits). Why: one behaviour per stop; a raised allowance must end the wait (U-052); no limit passed.

CE-7 Ask first: one card per stop (key credential:ask), filed only by the writer that set limits.asking {stopKey, requestId} with the version check, only when work needs it (a task run, a review, planning, the task check; not chat alone, not a job), the other credential can serve now and the caps have room for the waiting work's next call; its words from credential-words.ts, computed when shown. 'Use API key' re-reads the stop, writes limits.grant {to, stopKey, by: 'card', at} (version-checked; audit billing.grant), then: the waiting tasks of a session that still runs go back into it as its own tasks (d1109-starts-engine's readmit on the admit handle, which clears the runner's notAgain for them), a session that ended to wait goes on now as the person's start (personContinue: by 'person', the rest of its promise, its cap less what the ledger booked), a waiting plan is drafted, work outside a person's session stays ready for the next Start. The grant covers every project's tasks, their reviews and planning, the task check and chat until the stop ends, never the background jobs, and the option's consequence line says so ('All work and chat use your API key until 15:40: about CHF 0.90 for what waits now.'). 'Wait' closes the card and moves nothing, and at the stop's end nothing starts (the work is ready for the next Start: 'Nothing moves. After 15:40 the work runs at your next Start.'); the asking mark keeps the stop, so no second card comes; recordWait(source, stopKey) records the same answer without a card, for the Start dialog's 'Start at 15:40' under ask (d1109-cred-screens), so no card follows the person's own choice. A second or late answer changes nothing and returns the card's Done line; an answer after the stop ended grants nothing. The wake, before takeReady, ends grants whose stop is over and withdraws open cards whose stop ended, whose other credential cannot serve any more, or whose preset changed. Why: 'after asking human' as one card; answered once; restart-safe; no start the person did not ask for (D6).

CE-8 A refusal follows the rule and always informs: one card per refusal at a time, filed only by the writer that flips limits.refusedCard {refusedAt, open} to open with the version check (refuse() and noteWait's TR-10 path alike: concurrent refusals file one, and work that waits on the still-refused credential after the card was closed files it once more); closing the card clears open; refusalWhyOf(error) stores a category (expired sign-in, invalid or deleted key, not allowed for this model or workspace, other), never the provider's text; the card's body says what the work does under the rule (wait, next, or ask with Use API key / Wait, staying open as the fix-it card after an answer); a refused credential gets no second request from any path (a switch, a grant, a continuation, a late answer, chat, a job, the probe) until a different one is saved. Why: 7c; no retry that could lock the person's account.

decisions: 'fix the tasks' (and its synonyms, English and German) is recognised by the parser without a model call; the chat model gets one fix_tasks tool for the same request in other words. Why: no fast-model call before a planning-model call; one path.

The check, the fence and the autonomy rule are d1109-selftasks-run's: from Standard the changes are made by the agent (the planFix context: no read-back, no Inbox echo) and listed with an Undo each, unless a lookup in that turn returned records (d1109-chat-recall's recordsRead: then they are read back at every level); at Advisor and Assisted, or when the set asks first, one composed read-back with Yes and No. Why: the owner's 'autonomy level deciding when it asks first', the same in chat as in a run.

Changes the person names in their own words stay the person's instruction and are read back; several in one line become one question. Why: design §3.9's read-back holds for interpreted instructions; one question per line, never a second card left in the Inbox.
The session page gets an Undo on each change line, from the change log row the event names. Why: 'each change shown with one Undo' where the person sees it.
Changes shows 'In a session' and the agent's name for an agent's change; the task drawer shows what the agent did. Why: design §5 rule 3 (names) and 'every change shown'.
The suggestion card shows its changes open. Why: the person approves what they can read.

fix_tasks takes no request text from the model: its only parameter is the project; the code passes the person's message of that turn verbatim (at most 500 characters) as the request. Why: the design says the person's words are the request; a model-written request could carry text the person never said.

SC-12 (was ST-4): an agent's change says so where it is stored: task.ts's reasons 'Changed by the agent: …', 'Added by the agent: <why>', 'Split from "Style the page" by the agent', 'Dropped by the agent: same as "Add the README"'; never 'by you' for the agent, never an id or 'via chat'. Why: every change shown, plainly, by who made it (design §5 rule 3).

SC-13 (was ST-15): the critic's session review counts a task the agent split, or dropped as a duplicate, as replaced, not as planned and left undone. Why: a correct fix must not lower the plan's grade.

Add two tasks in chat, change one of them, write a note, then say 'run it now' and press Yes: only then does a session start; saying 'ok' or 'sounds good' starts nothing.

While a session runs, Redo a small done task: it says 'It joins the session that is running.' and runs before the session ends; Make ready a large one: it says it waits for your next Start and does not run.
In Settings, turn on 'When work is ready: Start a session by itself' for one project and answer a card there: a session starts; turn it off again.

If your Claude subscription reaches its limit during a session with 'then wait': the other tasks still run, then the session ends saying it waits until <time>; at that time nothing starts, the project says 'Ready: N tasks wait for your Start' and the session's Continue offers the rest with its budget left. Press Start before the reset instead and choose 'Start at <time>': the project says 'Starts at <time>' with Cancel, and it starts then.

In the tray menu, 'Stop all sessions' stops the running session and nothing starts until you choose 'Allow sessions again'.

Install the run C build (Desktop app workflow), keep the project at Standard, and give it a brief whose plan has a task that is clearly two jobs (for example 'Make a one-page site with a contact form, styled, and publish it'). Start. When a task's report says the task list needs a change, see on the session page one line per change with an Undo, and the new tasks on the Tasks tab with what they wait for.

Press Undo on one of those lines on the session page: see only that change taken back (the task as it was, the new part gone) and the others left; see the same row marked Undone in Changes, labelled 'In a session'.
At the session's end see one Update for it in the Inbox (with 'changed N tasks'), not one per change.

Set the project to Assisted (Settings, autonomy by name) and run another session: see one card 'the agent suggests N changes to the tasks' with the changes listed, the session going on meanwhile; press Make these changes and see one Changes row with one Undo; no new session starts by itself.

With a subscription-first choice in Settings, Basics, 'Which Claude does the work' (once d1109-cred-screens is in; before it, Settings, Advanced, 'Claude: which to use first'), run one session where a check happens: see the check's cost in CHF on the session page and the subscription allowance moving; nothing over the session budget. With no choice made, the check runs on the API key (money) even in a subscription session.
Check the money: with a small session budget, see work the agent added named under 'Left for your next Start' instead of run, and no session starting until you press Start.
Read every new line (session page, card, Update, chat, task drawer): one plain sentence each, CHF, no ids, no raw states.

Open Settings: Basics shows 'Which Claude does the work' under Accounts and keys with your earlier choice selected (or, if you never set an order, 'Not chosen yet: ...' with none selected), both credentials in order with their state now, and one line saying what happens if the first runs out. Pick 'Subscription first, ask before API key': it changes at once and Changes lists it with Undo. Pick 'Subscription first, then API key': a yes is asked first, saying it costs money.

With 'ask before API key', when your plan's limit is reached during a session: one Inbox card 'Use your API key until ...?' with the reset time in your time and the cost. Press Wait: your API key's spend in Settings and Costs does not move, and no second card comes for that limit; after the reset nothing starts until you press Start. At the next limit press Use API key: the session goes on at once, and the task's drawer, the session page and Costs -> By credential show the work on your API key with its cost. After the reset, the next tasks use your subscription again.

With 'Subscription first, then wait' and your subscription at its limit: nothing runs on the API key while it waits; chat says it has not answered and offers 'Use API key', which spends only when you press it; no reminder arrives while it waits.

The Start dialog and an unapproved plan card each say in one line what happens if your first choice runs out; with your subscription at its limit the Start dialog offers 'Use API key' and 'Start at 15:40'.
With a real Claude Code limit (the 5-hour or weekly one), the reset time on the card, the rows and the Start dialog matches what Claude Code reports.

open_questions.question: Should a session you started go on by itself when its Claude credential is back (the 5-hour or weekly reset, a raised allowance, a new key)?
open_questions.default_built: No. Its tasks read 'Ready: it runs at your next Start.', the session's Continue offers the rest with its budget left, and Start pressed during the wait ('Start at 15:40') makes it go on at that time.
open_questions.why: Your confirmed list puts 'a credential coming back' among what only prepares work; a reset can come hours or weeks later, while you may be giving instructions.

open_questions.question: With 'Start a session by itself' on for a project, should a pull request comment or a CI result also start a session?
open_questions.default_built: No. They reach the agent's inbox and the next session reads them.
open_questions.why: That text is written by someone else; it would start paid work, and the setting's yes line says 'when work you made ready can run'.

open_questions.question: The critic's monthly calibration runs on its own schedule (on by default, the 1st at 06:00, within its own monthly budget in Settings): keep it so, or run it only when you turn it on? Should it show in the bar that shows a running session?
open_questions.default_built: As today: on its schedule, not shown in the bar, its cost on Costs; named in the ADR as the one session nobody presses Start for.
open_questions.why: It is a session nobody starts by hand; it does no project work and never blocks Start, but it spends on the model.

open_questions.question: Should 'When work is ready: Start a session by itself' also have an app-wide default for new projects?
open_questions.default_built: Per project only, off for every project.
open_questions.why: One project can run hands-off while you are still shaping another.

open_questions.question: Your yes on 'Use your API key until …?' lets all work and chat in every project use the API key until your subscription is back, which for the weekly limit can be days. Keep that, or should a yes cover only the work waiting at that moment?
open_questions.default_built: The yes covers all work and chat until the stop ends (never the background jobs); the button says so, every later Start dialog says it runs on the key, and Settings has 'Stop using it'.
open_questions.why: One yes can mean days of spend on the key; the card's figure prices only the work waiting now.

open_questions.question: If you never chose an order, tasks use your subscription first but chat, planning, reviews and the agent's task check use your API key first (money per call, also inside a subscription session). Keep that split, or one order for every call, subscription first?
open_questions.default_built: The split is kept and named in Settings; picking any preset sets one order for every call.
open_questions.why: One order would move chat to Claude Code (a second or two slower; under 'wait' chat cannot answer until the reset).

open_questions.question: If you never chose what happens when your first Claude runs out, the rule is 'wait' (your default of 2026-11-02). Should it be 'ask first' now that it exists?
open_questions.why: 'Ask first' did not exist when you chose.

open_questions.question: One credential choice for all projects, or a per-project override?
open_questions.why: The credentials and the plan's limits are yours, shared by every project.

open_questions.question: Should the API key get its own monthly limit in Forerunner ('at most CHF 20 a month on the API key')?
open_questions.default_built: No: Anthropic's own spend limit and your monthly cap bound it; a limit stored by an earlier version still counts as running out.
open_questions.why: Not asked for yet; it would be a new limit in the hooks.

open_questions.question: Under 'Subscription first, then wait', the Start dialog and chat still offer a one-off 'Use API key' that spends only when you press it. Keep that, or offer it only under 'ask before API key'?
open_questions.why: 'Wait' means the app does nothing by itself, not that you cannot choose.

open_questions.question: The agent changes its own tasks without asking from Standard (the default level) and asks first at Advisor and Assisted. Keep that, or ask first up to Standard and change them alone only from Trusted?
open_questions.why: You said the autonomy level decides when it asks first, but not which level.

open_questions.question: A task you added or edited yourself: should the agent change it on its own from Standard, as it does its own tasks?
open_questions.default_built: It only suggests changes to your tasks (one card, your yes), at every level.
open_questions.why: Your own edit would otherwise be overwritten without asking.

open_questions.question: A task that failed after its tries: should its card also offer 'Split it'?
open_questions.default_built: The card stays as today (Try again, Mark done anyway, Cancel task); 'split X' in chat does it, read back.
open_questions.why: One more option on a card that already has three.

open_questions.question: Should 'Fix the tasks' also be a button on the Tasks tab?
open_questions.default_built: Chat only, plus the agent's own check during a run.
open_questions.why: One more button on the Tasks tab.

owner_explanation:
1. A session starts only when you say so: Start, Approve and start, Continue, Use API key on a card, or 'run it now' in chat, which is always asked back once.
2. Each project has an optional 'Start a session by itself' setting, off by default; only you can turn it on, and the agent's own tasks never start one.
3. Everything else only gets work ready: answers, Redo, Try again, Make ready, Resume, raised budgets and a Claude credential that is back.
4. Ready work joins a running session only if that session's budget still covers the tasks it promised at Start; otherwise it waits for your next Start.
5. Each action says in one line which of these happens. Nothing reminds you about waiting work.
6. While a session runs, one bar under the header on every page, in Talk, the browser tab, the window title and the tray shows the project, what it does and Stop.
7. If Claude runs out mid-session, the other tasks still run. When it is back nothing starts by itself: Continue offers the rest with the budget left, or press 'Start at 15:40' beforehand.
8. The agent keeps its own task list right during a run and when you say 'fix the tasks': rewording, splitting, adding a missing step, reordering, dropping a duplicate.
9. From Standard it makes each change and shows it with its own Undo; at Advisor and Assisted it asks first on one card. One Update per session.
10. It never touches a running task, a budget or another project, and pays its check only from budget the session's promise does not need.
11. Text in reports is never obeyed: a line that reads like an instruction is not passed to the model; the agent asks you and quotes it.
12. Which Claude does the work is one choice in Settings, Basics, from five options such as 'Subscription first, ask before API key'.
13. 'Ask' files one card with the cost; your yes lets all work and chat use the API key until your subscription is back. 'Wait' means nothing moves.
14. A refused credential follows the same choice, tells you once what was refused and how to fix it, and is never tried again until you save a new one.
15. Every switch shows on the task, the session and Costs with its CHF; no budget, cap or share is ever passed. Open questions list what is built meanwhile.
